lines.ruling: Ruling: scope; f1040 p. 1, "If joint return, spouse's first name"; amb.2025.filer_under_16. The roster test (one taxpayer; a spouse entry exactly on a joint return) is the project's; the project also carries household.roster_ok's under-16 refusal, which the reply bypasses. Every difference is that refusal (project-unknown on incomplete records, one project-refuses); none on a completed return. Project stands.

The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN" (amb.2025.ctc_spouse_itin_application). The reply requires person.tin of every filer, also of one who answered person.work_ssn Yes (an SSN valid for employment is an SSN), which the interview then does not ask: the 5 completed candidate-unknowns are class M records whose route-limited answers omit person.tin for such a filer (classm.s3.4, classm.s3.4.deepseek, classm.tcw.5, classm.tcw.2 spouse). Ruling: model error; i1040s8812 p. 2, Form 8862 may be required, "you must attach Form 8862 to your tax return to claim the CTC, ACTC, or ODC unless an exception applies" (Form 8862 is needed only to claim the credit). The candidate copies household.credit_disallowed, so it is true whenever the answer is Yes, also on a return that claims no child tax credit or credit for other dependents (Schedule 8812 line 8 not above line 11, where line 12 says "No. Stop here. You cannot take the child tax credit, credit for other dependents, or additional child tax credit"). The project tests line 8 above line 11 first and then the answer, which it now reads through its gate line household.credit_disallowed_if_claimed (asked only when the return claims one of the four credits). executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/household.json`; 1,638 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 235 partial records): no value difference on a completed return; 1 candidate-unknown on a completed return (the answer is withheld where the project does not need it); the other differences are refused or incomplete records. Same reading as the earlier ruling on this line (T-101). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 43, Form 8862, who must file, "You must file Form 8862 if your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed for any reason other than a math or clerical error" (to take the credit; the Reminder on p. 46, "to find out if you must file Form 8862 to take the credit for 2025"). The candidate copies household.credit_disallowed, so it is true on a return that takes no earned income credit. The project tests that the credit is claimed (Steps 1 to 5 passed and eic.line6, Worksheet A line 6 or Worksheet B line 11, above zero) and then the answer, read through its gate line household.credit_disallowed_if_claimed. executable-triage-v2 (`../triage/household.json`; 1,638 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 235 partial records): the value differences on completed returns are f2.t101.credit_disallowed_no_credit_claimed and f2.t101.credit_disallowed_eic_zero (answer Yes, no earned income credit claimed: project false, candidate true), the narrowing T-101 made; 3 candidate-unknown on completed returns (answer withheld where the project does not need it); the rest are refused or incomplete records. Project stands.

Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household: "Check the 'Head of household' box only if you are unmarried (or considered unmarried) and either Test 1 or Test 2 applies"; i1040gi p. 23 (amb.2025.hoh_community_property). The reply writes the project's test inline (status head of household, and the unmarried test fails or neither Test 1 nor Test 2 applies) and drops the household.hoh_community_property refusal the project carries on household.hoh_eligible; it reads household.unmarried as the project does.
